A uniformly charged disc of radius R having surface charge density σ\sigmaσ is placed in the xy plane with its center at the origin. Find the electric field intensity along the z-axis at a distance Z from origin :-
  1. (A)E=σ2ε0(1−Z(Z2+R2)1/2)E = \frac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}\left(1 - \frac{Z}{(Z^2 + R^2)^{1/2}}\right)E=2ε0​σ​(1−(Z2+R2)1/2Z​)
  2. (B)E=σ2ε0(1+Z(Z2+R2)1/2)E = \frac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}\left(1 + \frac{Z}{(Z^2 + R^2)^{1/2}}\right)E=2ε0​σ​(1+(Z2+R2)1/2Z​)
  3. (C)E=2ε0σ(1(Z2+R2)1/2+Z)E = \frac{2\varepsilon_0}{\sigma}\left(\frac{1}{(Z^2 + R^2)^{1/2}} + Z\right)E=σ2ε0​​((Z2+R2)1/21​+Z)
  4. (D)E=σ2ε0(1(Z2+R2)+1Z2)E = \frac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}\left(\frac{1}{(Z^2 + R^2)} + \frac{1}{Z^2}\right)E=2ε0​σ​((Z2+R2)1​+Z21​)

Correct answer: (A)
